intro: Using Chrome for social media analysts on Mac requires a balance of speed and organization. You can master your browser by leveraging specific keyboard shortcuts and managing multiple profiles to keep your brand accounts separate.
tldr: Use Chrome profiles to keep personal and professional social media accounts distinct.
Master keyboard shortcuts like ⌘ + T for new tabs and ⌘ + L for the address bar.
Install only necessary extensions to keep your browser fast.
Use Lazur to voice-control your browser and find specific elements on your screen.
Clear your cache regularly to prevent site loading errors.

blocks.text: Social media analysts often manage dozens of brand accounts. Logging in and out of Facebook, Instagram, or LinkedIn is a massive waste of time. Instead, use Chrome profiles. Go to your profile icon in the top right corner and select Add. This creates a separate instance of Chrome for each client or brand. You can even assign a different color theme to each profile so you know exactly which account you are working in.
Essential keyboard shortcuts for your Mac

items: ⌘ + T: Open a new tab instantly.
⌘ + L: Jump to the address bar to type a URL.
⌘ + ⇧ + T: Reopen the last closed tab if you accidentally exit a dashboard.
⌘ + Option + Right Arrow: Switch to the next tab in your current window.
⌘ + F: Open the find bar to search for specific keywords on a webpage.

blocks.text: How Lazur helps your social media workflow

Lazur lives in the notch of your Mac. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask questions about anything on your screen. If you are stuck in a complex analytics dashboard and cannot find the export button, ask Lazur where it is. It will draw a circle around the button for you. If you need to write a quick response to a comment, hold fn to dictate your reply directly into the text field. It keeps your hands on the keyboard and your focus on the content.
Keeping your browser fast and clean

A cluttered browser slows down your Mac. If you notice Chrome lagging, check your extensions. Go to Chrome > Settings > Extensions and remove anything you do not use daily. You should also clear your cache if a site is acting up. Go to Chrome > Clear Browsing Data and select the time range you want to wipe. This often fixes the dreaded Aw Snap error that happens during heavy research sessions.

You likely use tools like Buffer, Later, or Sprout Social. Do not keep these tabs lost in a sea of other pages. Right-click any tab in the tab bar and select Pin. This keeps your most important tools on the far left of your browser. They will stay there even after you close and reopen Chrome. This makes switching between your scheduling tool and your analytics dashboard much faster.

items: Leaving dozens of unused tabs open for days. Close them to save memory.
Installing too many extensions. They consume system resources and can slow down page loads.
Ignoring Chrome updates. Always keep your browser on the latest version for security.
Using the same profile for personal and work accounts. This leads to accidental posts on the wrong handle.

blocks.text: What to do next for your workflow

Start by creating a dedicated profile for each brand you manage. Once that is done, pin your primary dashboard tabs to the left side of your browser. If you find yourself repeating the same tasks, look into how you can use voice commands to speed up your input. Your goal is to spend less time managing the browser and more time creating content.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate apps for you. It points at them or guides you through the steps.

faq.question: How do I update Chrome on my Mac?
faq.answer: Click the three dots in the top right, go to Help, and select About Google Chrome. It will check for updates automatically.

faq.question: Is Lazur safe to use with my client data?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur only looks at your screen while you hold the shortcut, and the data is not stored or used to train models.
